LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 8.1.1 LISTENING AND RESPONDING: ORAL NARRATIVES - MYTHS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.1: Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths, part of Strand 8 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you tell what is going to happen in a story? 2. How are the characters or events in the story related to the people or happenings around us?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the characters in a given myth,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. narrate the key events in a given myth,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain the moral lesson in a set myth,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. relate the characters in a myth to real life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the role/importance of oral literature in lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the characters in a given myth,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. narrate the key events in a given myth,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain the moral lesson in a set myth,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. relate the characters in a myth to real life,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. acknowledge the role/importance of oral literature in lifelong learning.

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. predict events in a myth from the title or pictures in the story,

2. listen to a narration of a myth from your community then retell the myth to their peers,

3. watch a video recording of a myth,

4. identify the characters in the myth,

5. collaborate answer questions from the story,

6. discuss the lessons learnt from a myth,

7. discuss the relevance of the story to real life. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. predict events in a myth from the title or pictures in the story,
2. listen to a narration of a myth from your community then retell the myth to their peers,
3. watch a video recording of a myth,
4. identify the characters in the myth,
5. collaborate answer questions from the story,
6. discuss the lessons learnt from a myth,
7. discuss the relevance of the story to real life. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: It is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology through video recording of a myth.

• Collaboration: It is enhanced as the learner respects the rules of engagement when discussing the moral lesson of a story with

peers.

Values:
Respect: It is developed as the learner listens to and appreciates myths from different communities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: It is enhanced as the learner interacts with stories from various communities.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner relates myths and other types of narratives to other learning areas such as Religious Education.

2. narrate the key events in a given myth,
3. explain the moral lesson in a set myth,
4. relate the characters in a myth to real life,
5. acknowledge the role/importance of oral literature in lifelong learning.
